column1: # manifests/scaffold.tsv — every file the scaffolder is allowed to copy.
# WHY THIS IS DATA AND NOT CODE. The two-layer boundary (docs/layers.md) says
# core must never read, copy, or execute anything on the sample shelf. A rule
# lives only inside scripts/setup.sh is a rule nobody can see being broken:
# one added `cp` line and the sample shelf has become a default. Pulling the
# copy list out as data makes a boundary violation show up in the diff, and
# lets the acceptance gate (test group H) assert on it directly.
# STATUS: LIVE. scripts/setup.sh reads this file and copies exactly these rows
# — there is no second copy list anywhere in the script. Add a row and the
# scaffolder copies it; delete one and it stops. The validation rules below are
# enforced by setup.sh itself (a bad row is exit 2, never a silently skipped
# line) and asserted again by test group H.
#   source <TAB> dest <TAB> guard
#   source  path of the file to copy, relative to the REPO ROOT
#   dest    path to create, relative to the SCAFFOLD TARGET ($TARGET in
#           setup.sh — the repo root itself by default)
#   guard   when the copy is skipped:
#             skip-if-exists                     dest already exists
#             skip-if-any-exists:A,B             any of A,B exists at the
#                                                target root (never clobber
#                                                an agent-instructions file)
#   Blank lines and lines whose first non-space character is `#` are comments.
# ─── VALIDATION RULES (what a checker must enforce) ────────────────────────
#   1. exactly 3 tab-separated fields per data row; no leading/trailing space
#   2. source MUST be relative and MUST start with `templates/`
#   3. dest   MUST be relative; MUST NOT start with `/`
#   4. NO `..` path segment anywhere, in any field
#   5. the sample-shelf prefix — the word cook·book followed by a slash — must
#      not appear ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE, comments included. Not in a field, not
#      in a note, not in an example. This is the machine form of the one-way
#      dependency rule, and it is kept absolute on purpose: a checker that has
#      to tell a "real" path from a "merely quoted" one is a checker with an
#      argument in it. Nothing here needs to name that directory; if you need
#      to explain the boundary, link docs/layers.md instead. (That is also why
#      this very rule spells the word with a separator.)
#   6. every source MUST exist in the repo
#   7. no duplicate dest
# ─── DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS MANIFEST ─────────────────────────────────────
# These are things setup.sh does that are NOT source->dest template copies,
# listed here so their absence reads as a decision rather than an omission:
#   · mkdir only, no content: ssot/ briefs/ logs/ local/ projects/_archive/
#     judgment/mining/ judgment/reports/ judgment/logs/
#   · config.env.example -> config.env — the source is NOT under templates/,
#     so it cannot be a row here without weakening validation rule 2. It is a
#     machine-local config seed, not a template.
#   · judgment/correction_patterns.txt — created by setup.sh from a heredoc, not
#     copied from anywhere, and containing COMMENTS ONLY. It is not a row here
#     because there is no template to copy: the phrases you type when you
#     overrule an agent cannot be shipped, and the scanner refuses to run until
#     you write your own.
#   · templates/promotion_candidate.md — read by scripts/distill.sh and pasted
#     into the prompt it fires. It is a format definition the machinery consumes
#     in place, not a file the user fills in, so it is not scaffolded.
#   · templates/correction_patterns.example.txt,
#     templates/discipline_catalog.example.yaml, templates/distill-prompt.md,
#     templates/discipline-audit-prompt.md, templates/inbound_sweep.md
#     — NOT scaffolded, on purpose. Copying a menu to the path a scanner reads
#     would make a shipped vocabulary everyone's default without anyone
#     choosing it. The act of copying is where the user chooses. See
#     docs/layers.md, "why the copying is left to the user".
#   · templates/starter-disciplines.md — same rule, and now also the wrong
#     layer: the burned-discipline menu is somebody's CONTENT, so it moved to
#     the sample shelf and this path is a signpost stub. Not scaffolded before
#     the move, not scaffolded after. See docs/layers.md and
#     docs/path-migrations.md.
